statement: The function returns a result r and len(r) = n - k + 1. For every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, r[i] = max { nums[j] | 0 <= j < n and i <= j <= i + k - 1 }, i.e. r[i] is the maximum of the contiguous window of length k starting at index i.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n - k + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1 and every j with i <= j <= i + k - 1, we have r[i] >= nums[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1 there exists j with i <= j <= i + k - 1 such that r[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the maximum of all entries of r equals the maximum of all entries of nums: max(r[0], ..., r[len(r)-1]) = max(nums[0], ..., nums[n-1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), min(nums[0], ..., nums[n-1]) <= r[i] <= max(nums[0], ..., nums[n-1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Let m = n - k + 1. Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices t_0, ..., t_{m-1} such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, i <= t_i <= i + k - 1 and r[i] = nums[t_i], and moreover t_0 <= t_1 <= ... <= t_{m-1}.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.

statement: Let m = n - k + 1. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < m - 1: (a) if r[i+1] < r[i] then r[i] = nums[i]; and (b) if r[i+1] > r[i] then r[i+1] = nums[i+k].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100000, every nums[j] for 0 <= j < n lies in [-10000, 10000], and k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= n.
